notes:
I couldn't write any notes this time. The research tool hit its usage limit before it loaded a single page, so I have nothing from Enduring Word, Bible Hub (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit), Precept Austin, the NET Bible notes or any of the other approved sites.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and to leave out anything I couldn't find. Since I found nothing, I haven't written any verse notes. Filling them in from my own memory would give you uncited claims you couldn't check.

When the tool is available again, I'll work in this order:
1. **Main verse-by-verse sources:** Enduring Word on Isaiah 26; the Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit and Wesley notes on Bible Hub; and Precept Austin's Isaiah 26 page.
2. **Modern scholarship:** the NET Bible notes on Isaiah 26, which matter most for the hard verses: v. 3 ("perfect peace"), v. 14 compared with v. 19, and v. 19's "dew."
3. **Where traditions differ:** mainly v. 19 (whether it teaches bodily resurrection or speaks of the nation being restored) and v. 20 (whether "hide yourselves" is read as a rapture). I'll look for these on the Reformed, Baptist, Wesleyan, Pentecostal and Lutheran sites.
4. **Catholic and Orthodox readings:** New Advent (the Church Fathers on v. 19), Catholic.com and OCA.org. Isaiah 26 is also among the Old Testament readings in the Orthodox Matins service.
5. **Popular modern teaching:** only if a site actually discusses it, for example "perfect peace" in v. 3 or "all that we have accomplished, You have done" in v. 12.

Each point will have its URL, and anything I can't find will be left out.
